body:
m1 - CANDIDATE d9d7d97 on m1/blend-support, base 855b754. Ready to gate.

GATE: align 200 on JVM, JS and Native; codec 107 on JVM and JS; fixtures 116; scalafmtCheckAll run LAST, clean.

THE KEY-COUNT RECONCILIATION YOU ASKED FOR, and it came out exact:

  old 44a76b728b8dfc7474536cc17aed9f7a2718116f672711c2c0cb773c989b9ba9   25,294 bytes
  new 32f509c93358ae7d8748c5d7f940c4ff69db33ceac78eb61073ec0dff43bab2f   25,960 bytes

  DELTA 666 BYTES = 18 NEW supportWeight KEYS x 37 BYTES, EXACTLY.

I checked WHY it divides evenly rather than reporting a suspiciously round average: the encoder writes doubles as CANONICAL HEX BIT PATTERNS, so every key is the same width - 36 characters plus a comma. Two distinct values appear, 0x3ff0000000000000 which is exactly 1.0 on ten cells, and 0x3fee9131abf0b767 which is 0.9552 on eight. So the entire byte delta is accounted for by keys I can name, and nothing else in the artifact moved. That is the substitute for eyeballing 25KB, and I think it is stronger than eyeballing would have been.

All seven canaries re-run and green. JVM/JS-versus-Native split untouched.

TWO THINGS I VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED:
  - supportWeight is NOT INERT. On the worked example it takes exactly two values, 1.0 and 0.9552,
    the latter being 3.2/3.35 to four places - the eligible-support fraction of a five-term cell,
    appearing on precisely the two units with no sensory term. Had it been 1.0 everywhere the whole
    change would have been theatre.
  - the two SignatureSuite literals were RE-DERIVED against 855b754, not carried over. Identical to
    my pre-rebase measurement, so the scout's landing and mine are orthogonal - checked on both
    sides of the rebase because I had predicted they might interact.

AND ONE PLACE THE TESTS CORRECTED ME. I wrote that mean-of-ratios would not move, reasoning it
depends on localizability alone. Wrong: WHICH ROWS ARE LOCALIZABLE is a function of the posterior.
It moved 0.628359 -> 0.635733. I have pinned the GAP as well now, 0.049861 -> 0.051288, so a change
that moves both formulas together fails there rather than passing an inequality.

STILL TRUE AND WORTH REPEATING AT THE GATE: this is an imputation. It assumes unmeasured eligible
terms behave like measured ones. The difference from what it replaces is that it is named, recorded
per cell, carried on the wire, and refusable - not that it assumes nothing.
